name: Nguyen Dang
about: I am currently the Lead Global Engagement Fellow at the Open Society University Network (OSUN), where I work to foster international collaboration in education and social impact. Since 2017, I have been actively engaged in social projects related to education, cultural preservation, job orientation, and environmental issues. Through these initiatives, I have worked with diverse communities, developing programs that empower individuals and promote sustainable development. I have a strong research interest in political science, international security, peace, and international relations, particularly in areas related to diplomacy, conflict resolution, and policy-making. Professional Experience in Psychology & Social Support: I have gained diverse experience in the psychology and well-being field, focusing on mental health, education, and behavioral development: 🔹 Wellness Ambassador | Fulbright Wellness Center At Fulbright University Vietnam, I served as a Wellness Ambassador, where I designed and facilitated student well-being programs. My work involved mental health advocacy, peer support training, and organizing workshops on stress management, mindfulness, and emotional resilience. I also worked closely with the university’s counseling team to create a supportive environment for students. 🔹 Research Assistant | Ho Chi Minh City University of Education (HCMUE) - HCMC National University As a Research Assistant, I contributed to a research project titled "Promoting Well-Being at School", funded by MOET through HCMC University of Education (HCMUE). My responsibilities included conducting interviews, gathering and analyzing qualitative data, and making reports. 🔹 Intern | Learning Strategies At Learning Strategies, a specialized center supporting children with cognitive, behavioral, and developmental challenges, I worked as an intern assisting psychologists and educators, hosting social events. The center provides tailored interventions for children diagnosed with autism, ADHD, and other learning disabilities. My role involved supporting therapy sessions, organizing group events, and assisting in developing educational strategies to help children improve their social, academic and other skills. Through my combined experiences in policy research, education, and psychology, I am committed to fostering inclusive and impactful solutions that address social challenges on both local and global scales.

recommendations: ["Brody Rolston “Throughout the course of my academic career, I’ve come to realize that oftentimes one’s classroom conduct can offer deep insight into their moral beliefs, work ethic, and, above all, their character. It is through this lens that I’ve come to see Tina as the inspiring creative and unparalleled leader that she is. Tina and I have spent the last 5 months together in Cranbrook’s Entrepreneurial Leadership class, a class tailored toward students well-versed in both business skills and community service. Throughout the course, we’ve worked toward creating Youth Inc, a social enterprise with the mission of providing young entrepreneurs with the skills and resources to create their own businesses. From the very beginning of the entrepreneurial process, Tina stood out with a constant desire to build on existing ideas as well as her own. A major portion of developing Youth Inc. was to make a slide deck that could be presented to several potential partners in the city of Detroit. However, our group struggled with presenting our ideas and information in a concise, easy-to-understand manner. Tina was our solution. Without hesitation, she took the lead on designing our presentation by merging both her artistic sense and communication with other classmates to ultimately create a PowerPoint that has already astounded multiple Detroit-based entrepreneurs, such as Tom Lewand who has been helping to revitalize Marygrove College. Without Tina’s hard work, none of this would have been possible. Her ability to connect with those that she works with is rivaled only by her incredible leadership style. When I first met Tina, we had the assignment to get to know one other person in the room. I was paired with Tina. From that conversation, I learned what is probably my deepest insight into Tina: her leadership style makes others feel like they’re at home. She helps people become confident in themselves, become driven to contribute to whatever it is that they’re working on, and become the best possible version of themselves. In writing this, I find myself worrying that others will see this as being too good to be true, but I firmly believe that everything I’ve said is completely true. Tina's achievements mean all the more given the context that Entrepreneurial Leadership is a class comprised primarily of Seniors whereas she is currently a Junior. From my own experience, I’ve seen that oftentimes juniors in classes filled with seniors sink into the background, too intimidated to offer their own ideas and insights as the rest of the class appears to be wiser, more qualified, and ultimately more worthy of participating. However, the opposite is true of Tina. As mentioned before, Tina had no problems integrating herself into the class and becoming a key component of the classroom atmosphere. After 2017, my new job at BP Store encouraged me to be more technical, and I worked for a computer and video game brand that enriched my knowledge of filmmaking software and compatible hardware. I learned to create engaging content online by incorporating VFX elements and producing fresh and innovative content to better engage the Vietnamese audience with brands. In 2021, I founded my own freelance service, Box98, specializing specifically in music videos and advertisement videos, which fortunately gained traction with a hit in 2021, garnering almost 17 million views on YouTube, along with several other moderately successful music videos and commercial projects. name: Yewie L.
about: I am a young entrepreneur and finance educator passionate about building a practical, behavior-driven investment education ecosystem for Vietnam’s Gen Z. I founded Genstock, an education platform that equips students with real-world investing skills — starting with fundamental and technical analysis, and expanding into financial literacy, behavioral finance, and real investing experience. Genstock was born from my belief that academic theory must be complemented by real-world readiness. While universities focus on essential frameworks, I focus on helping students develop the mindsets, practical skills, and emotional discipline that are critical in the finance and investment industry. To bring this vision to life, I collaborate with investment professionals, run a student-managed fund, and build a national network of finance clubs to co-create impactful, hands-on learning journeys. Currently, Genstock offers: - Flagship courses in stock analysis (fundamental & technical) - Workshops, and speaker events across major universities - A growing community of Gen Z investors supported by gamified learning and peer collaboration In parallel, I serve as the President of the BUV Investing Club, which I’ve helped transform into one of the university’s top academic clubs. Under my leadership, the club joined the International Finance Student Association (IFSA) and built strong partnerships with leading investment clubs at FTU, NEU, DAV, and AOF. I’m actively seeking meaningful collaborations to expand Genstock’s impact. I’m especially interested in connecting with: - University finance clubs: I offer free training for core teams, exclusive discounts for members, and the opportunity to co-host workshops, simulations, and speaker events tailored to student needs. - Industry professionals: I welcome partnerships with those willing to share practical, experience-based insights with the next generation of investors. - Researchers & media partners: I aim to co-create relatable, research-driven content that speaks to Gen Z combining financial literacy with behavior-based learning models. - NGOs & government organizations: I’m looking to contribute to broader financial inclusion and youth empowerment efforts across Vietnam and Southeast Asia. If you share a vision for empowering Gen Z through real, relevant financial education — let’s connect.

I'm currently interested in backend development with Go and Java, applying these skills through projects like building a compiler in Go and developing RESTful APIs for a backend web server. I want to work with teams who understand a group of people and develop products that enhance the convenience of their lives, backed by robust, efficient systems.

My academic journey is complemented by hands-on experience in research, software development, and hardware optimization, allowing me to bridge theory and practice effectively. Highlights of my journey include: - Co-authoring research on energy-aware resource allocation for wireless sensor nodes, published in IEEE Communications Letters. - Developing predictive maintenance models for electric vehicles using advanced machine learning techniques. - Exploring semantic communication and DeepJSCC (Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding) to enhance data transmission efficiency. I thrive in dynamic environments that challenge me to think creatively and innovate. With expertise in Python, C++, MATLAB, TensorFlow, and PyTorch, I have contributed to diverse projects, from building neural networks from scratch to designing IoT systems for smart aquaculture. My ultimate goal is to contribute to groundbreaking advancements in AI and engineering through impactful research roles. I am eager to work in environments where I can apply my skills to investigate complex problems, develop innovative solutions, and push the boundaries of what technology can achieve. Let’s connect and discuss how we can create impactful solutions together!

publications: [{"date":"January 14, 2025","description":"Low harvested energy poses a significant challenge to sustaining continuous communication in energy harvesting (EH)-powered wireless sensor networks. This is mainly due to intermittent and limited power availability from radio frequency signals. In this paper, we introduce a novel energy-aware resource allocation problem aimed at enabling the asynchronous accumulate-then-transmit protocol, offering an alternative to the extensively studied harvest-then-transmit approach. Specifically, we jointly optimize power allocation and time fraction dedicated to EH to maximize the average long-term system throughput, accounting for both data and energy queue lengths. By leveraging inner approximation and network utility maximization techniques, we develop a simple yet efficient iterative algorithm that guarantees at least a local optimum and achieves long-term utility improvement. Numerical results highlight the proposed approach’s effectiveness in terms of both queue length and sustained system throughput.","subtitle":"IEEE","title":"Energy-Aware Resource Allocation for Energy Harvesting Powered Wireless Sensor Nodes"}]

about: I'm an Economics student at Fulbright University Vietnam, with a growing passion for understanding how people interact, especially within business environments. My academic interests lie in the behavioral side of economics, where data meets human behavior, and decisions are influenced not just by numbers but also by relationships, communication, and context. At university, I’m developing a strong foundation in macroeconomic analysis, econometrics, and social research methods. This academic path, combined with my curiosity about real-world behavior, inspires me to take on a hands-on role that involves direct client-facing, such as that of my first job as a Sales Agent. Throughout my studies and work experience, I’ve focused on both analyzing data and gaining insight into customer engagement and market feedback. I believe that by bridging analytical thinking with strong interpersonal skills, businesses can greatly improve client relationship management, therefore increasing business efficiency. I’m currently seeking new opportunities—internships or projects—where I can apply and expand these skills, learn from industry professionals, and continue exploring how people, markets, and businesses connect and grow together.

about: As a final-year Business Management student at RMIT University Vietnam, I have spent the past few years exploring different aspects of the business world, particularly in marketing and media. Since February 2022, I have been a Media Member at SIFE RMIT Vietnam, where I have played a key role in leveraging media to communicate our organization’s values and goals. Through this experience, I honed my skills in content creation, digital communication, and audience engagement. However, as I progressed in my studies and professional exposure, I developed a growing enthusiasm for Business Intelligence and Data Analytics. I became increasingly fascinated by how data-driven insights could enhance strategic decision-making, optimize operations, and create measurable business impact. This realization has led me to pivot my career focus towards data analytics, business intelligence, and data-driven strategy. Now, as I approach graduation in June 2025, I am actively seeking opportunities to apply my analytical mindset and problem-solving skills in real-world business scenarios. I am particularly eager to explore internship opportunities in Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, and Data-Driven Strategy, where I can bridge my business acumen with my passion for analytics.

publications: [{"date":"October 13, 2024","description":"Service robots that work alongside humans in a shared environment need a navigation system that takes into account not only physical safety but also social norms for mutual cooperation. In this paper, we introduce a motion planning system that includes human states such as positions and velocities and their personal space for social-aware navigation. The system first extracts human positions from the LiDAR and the RGB-D camera. It then uses the Kalman filter to fuse that information for human state estimation. An asymmetric Gaussian function is then employed to model human personal space based on their states. This model is used as the input to the dynamic window approach algorithm to generate trajectories for the robot. Experiments show that the robot is able to navigate alongside humans in a dynamic environment while respecting their physical and psychological comfort.","subtitle":"IEEE","title":"Socially Aware Motion Planning for Service Robots Using LiDAR and RGB-D Camera"}]

name: Dang Minh Quang
city: Ho Chi Minh City Metropolitan Area
about: He stepped into advertising torn between a passion for its potential and the fear of not being good enough. Paralyzed by self-doubt, he watched from the sidelines as others thrived. But his frustration with the endless stream of bad advertising soon outweighed his fear. Inspired by the few great campaigns that truly connected with people, he realized admiring from afar wasn’t enough. He had to join the fight to create more meaningful work for the advertising world. Though he dreamed of being a strategic planner, he started with an account role. The position taught him the crucial lessons of precision and the challenges of flawless execution. At the same time, he proactively sought out strategy tasks, learning the "why" behind the "how." That's when it all clicked: to defeat bad advertising, brilliant strategy and flawless execution had to work as one. His dream was no longer about a job title; it transformed into a mission. A mission to become a brave warrior, fighting to bring creativity, meaning, and effectiveness back to local and global advertising. And so, he entered the arena, a place where brilliant dreams battled daily against the forces of cynicism and compromise. He was ready to fight for the former, and navigate the latter.

name: Akira Yanagisawa
about: My name is Akira Yanagisawa, I am an international student of senior year in Tourism and Hospitality Management at RMIT University Vietnam. I have become very interested in Vietnam after spending a holiday in the country since I was a teenager. In 2019, after careful considerations, I decided to move to Vietnam with a commitment to learn from one of the best international institutions in the world and build a career in the hospitality in a country which I consider as my second home. Over the past three years, I've challenged myself in various part-time roles including administrative, food services, and teaching while I was able to maintain a consistent academic performance at the university. My experiences in diverse environments have taught me to be flexible and inclusive, and I have learned about working with people from different backgrounds. Within the hospitality industry, my passion is to provide pleasant surprises and pleasure to our guests while developing the traditional Japanese spirit of hospitality (Omotenashi) on an international scale.

name: Minh Duc Ha
about: Minh Duc is a recently graduated student at the British University Vietnam (BUV), pursuing a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Marketing Management awarded by Staffordshire University. He completed an internship as a Sales Assistant at Secret Indochina Destination Management Company, where he gained hands-on experience exploring Vietnam’s lesser-known destinations - both professionally and personally. In the tourism industry, Duc has worked with English-speaking travelers, assisted in developing culturally rooted travel experiences, conducted supplier inspections, and built meaningful connections with everyone from ethnic homestay hosts to spiritual leaders. His core interests lie in sustainable tourism, ethical development, and the preservation of Vietnamese culture, beyond surface-level tourism trends. Duc’s journey into tourism is also deeply personal. Growing up, his father rarely had the opportunity to travel for leisure, often serving as the family’s "private chauffer" or traveling solely for work. Duc sees his own travels as a way of honoring and sharing that experience: “Every journey I take, I take for both of us.” He is now seeking opportunities in Marketing, Travel & Tourism, and Hospitality, where he can continue creating value through people-centered, culturally respectful, and community-driven work. about:
My name is Phuong Tran, a soon-to-be graduate who is deeply passionate about creating long-lasting and scalable solutions for young generations through education. I strongly believe that education and a learning mindset are the keys to a fulfilling career and personal life. I am also convinced that technology has the power to help people and ideas reach their full potential.

In my approach, I follow a problem-solving approach to realize the opportunities and possible scale of impacts. Also, I am constantly sharpening my thinking and growth mindset to enhance my core capabilities and welcome new ideas.

I have explored and experienced different aspects and formats of education throughout my journey to meet such passion. I have worked in positions in startup support, community sharing, e-learning services, and college app consulting. These experiences have allowed me to develop a well-rounded skillset that includes project management, leadership, research and analysis, team collaboration, and communication.

If you are interested in discussing topics related to education, emerging technologies, and personal development, I would be thrilled to connect with you via LinkedIn, or my email @ tranphuong.workspace@gmail.com.

Look forward to exchanging ideas with you!

name: Huong Binh Nguyen Vo
about: Hi! My name is Binh! I’m a marketer at heart, driven by the belief that authentic connections between brands and people are built through meaningful, impactful stories. My story start from a young age, I was captivated by the power of stories. I would marvel at how brands could weave narratives that not only captured attention but also built trust and loyalty. It was this fascination that drew me into the world of marketing, where I quickly realized that marketing is much more than just selling—it’s about connecting people, ideas, and experiences. Along my journey, I’ve been fortunate to meet incredible, inspiring individuals who’ve shown me just how transformative the field of marketing can be. These connections opened my eyes to new possibilities, helping me understand how deeply marketing impacts not only businesses but society as a whole. Through working on various projects, I’ve had the opportunity to explore different industries, cultures, and perspectives, each one broadening my view of the world. Whether it’s developing a campaign that resonates with a target audience or collaborating with a team to bring a brand’s vision to life, I’ve learned that marketing is a bridge—one that connects ideas to action and brings stories to life. Every step in my career has reaffirmed my belief that being a marketer is more than just a job—it’s a journey of continuous learning, growth, and exploration. I’m excited to continue building meaningful relationships, expanding my network, and helping brands tell their stories in authentic and impactful ways. Marketing has opened doors to incredible opportunities and allowed me to see the world through a unique lens, and I can’t wait to see where this adventure takes me next!!! :>

name: Luong Nguyen
about: At my core, I’m a builder, someone who finds joy in solving tough problems and turning ideas into real, working things. Whether it’s through code, data, or design, I’m driven by curiosity and the challenge of making things smarter, faster, or just plain better. My work sits at the intersection of AI and full-stack development. I’ve spent a lot of time in the world of NLP, and more recently I’ve been exploring computer vision and how machines interpret the world around them. I’m especially interested in how we can use data and AI to make thoughtful, meaningful decisions at scale. On the product side, I enjoy bringing systems to life, building user-friendly, performant applications end-to-end, from backend logic to pixel-perfect frontends. Outside of work? I’m a collector, a tinkerer, and a lifelong fan of anything with gears, bricks, or panels, LEGO, books, games, Gundam kits, model railroads, manga... basically anything that comes in pieces and needs putting together. I’m always up for working with curious minds who like to build cool stuff and push ideas forward. Let’s make something awesome.

name: Anh Hoang
about: I’m the kind of person who believes that trying something new - even if it scares me a little, is usually worth it. It’s how I’ve found myself navigating across fields, learning from unlikely sources, and gradually discovering what truly excites and fulfills me. I value people, process, and purpose (though which one takes the lead often depends on the day and the challenge at hand). I’ve learned that growth often hides in the most unexpected places, and that meaningful progress isn’t always loud or linear. Sometimes it looks like asking the right question, making a small adjustment, or just showing up with a better attitude. Along the way, I’ve come to appreciate the balance between taking things seriously and not taking myself too seriously. Staying curious, listening closely, and remembering to laugh - these are the tools I carry with me, whether I’m learning something new or helping others do the same.

name: Trong Nghia Nguyen
city: District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
about:
Hi, I’m Po – an Art & Media Studies student at Fulbright University Vietnam with a multidisciplinary approach to storytelling, cultural research, and strategic planning.

My work sits at the intersection of arts, urban culture, and global exchange. I’ve researched and documented grassroots street food economies, explored post-war legacies through cross-cultural filmmaking with Harvard and Dartmouth students, and contributed to public dialogue on Vietnam’s evolving creative identity, most recently through event planning and curating talks on the Vietnamese New Wave in cinema.

Beyond creative production, I also bring a strategic lens to cultural work. I’ve worked as a content and event strategist—designing meaningful experiences, writing scripts, and shaping narratives that resonate with both local and international audiences. I aim to connect insight-driven storytelling with impactful planning, especially in marketing, branding, and creative consultancy.

With experiences spanning Vietnam, the U.S., and Taiwan, I’m passionate about intercultural collaboration, urban storytelling, and how creative industries can shape more inclusive futures. Let's connect with you always open to conversations, co-creation, or consulting opportunities.

name: Son Chu
about: Over the past 2 years, I have gained valuable experience in business development, marketing, social media, and sales through my various RMIT University specialized courses, extra activities, and work experiences. During my business development internships in Haravan, I had the opportunity to work closely with the sales and marketing teams, identifying new business opportunities, conducting market research, and developing strategic plans to expand the company's reach. I learned how to analyze market trends, assess customer needs, and leverage competitive intelligence to create effective business strategies. In terms of marketing, I have developed a deep understanding of various marketing techniques and channels through RMIT volunteer programs and club activities and currently a social media officer for the physical therapy clinic Bonedoc). I have assisted marketing campaigns, conducted market research, and implemented digital marketing strategies. I have hands-on experience with tools such as social media advertising, content creation, email marketing, and search engine optimization (SEO) throughout RMIT's courses (specifically Marketing Intelligence, Social Media Management and Digital Content Creation). Correspondingly, I have developed content calendars, created engaging posts, and monitored analytics to measure the impact of social media efforts. I have gained insights into building online communities, driving user engagement, and leveraging social media as a powerful marketing tool. Furthermore, my experiences in sales internships at Anh Kim Real Estates have allowed me to hone my negotiation and relationship-building skills. I have learned to identify and qualify leads, conduct effective sales presentations, and close deals. I understand the importance of building long-term customer relationships and providing exceptional customer service to ensure customer satisfaction. Overall, my industry knowledge, and skill set in business development, marketing, social media, and sales internships have equipped me with a comprehensive understanding of these fields. I am confident in my ability to contribute to the success of any organization by leveraging my skills and experiences to drive growth, engage customers, and achieve business objectives.

name: Hà Nguyễn Minh Đoan Thùy (Hazel)
about: I was never the loudest in the room, but I was always paying attention. From a young age, I found comfort in details: arranging, planning, curating. While others raced ahead, I was the one quietly making sure everything held together. I chose Tourism & Hospitality Management at university not just for the love of service, but for the art of it - the invisible threads that hold all experiences together. It was through club activities and student projects that a sense of contributing to community began to grow in me, leading me to the Australian Hospitality Alumni Network Vietnam and, eventually, The Brand Promise in 2024. There, I began to sharpen my strength in project management: planning with care, and bringing creative visions into reality with diligent execution. Not long after, life offered a detour: a chance to work at Club Med as a G.O. It was unlike anything I had done before, and exactly what I needed. I returned with a softer perspective and a clearer sense of self. Today, I balance two roles. I am currently a Project Manager at The Brand Promise, where I focus on delivering effective outcomes that support our clients in reaching their professional goals. I also work as Head of Operations at Beyoutiful, a new lifestyle business that allows me to keep learning, building, and evolving from the ground up. My path has never been about rushing. It has always been about growing into the work I believe in, and the person I am choosing to become.

By putting people first, I create designs that make a difference in their lives. I believe in the power of design to greatly impact people and I exercise that power sensibly through creating accessible, inclusive, versatile, and sustainable designs. I take a multi-disciplinary approach to creativity, constantly learning from various creative fields to broaden my perspective and knowledge. By layering these diverse lenses, I aim to craft designs that are not only visually compelling but also comprehensive and well-rounded.

name: Nguyen Huy Hoang
city: District 7, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
about: Hoàng Nguyễn-Huy holds a BA degree in Social Studies from Fulbright University Vietnam. As an anthropologist in training, his research focuses on the figure of the non-humans in anthropology and how they relate to larger ecological relations and the process of worlding or building world(s). At the intersection of theoretical tenets such as nature-culture, myth, religion, ecology, and cosmopolitics, Hoàng's bachelor thesis examines flows of ontological ambiguity surrounding the Holy Whale (Cá Ông) as worshipped by fishermen in Quy Nhơn, Vietnam. Charting what he calls “anthropology of thoughts,” he aims to investigate differences at the fundamental level of thought while treating ‘thought’ as an ethnographic artifact with aesthetic affordances. His practices are therefore located in(-between) the formal indistinction between theory and practice, anthropology and philosophy. Hoàng has published his work on related themes in Anthways 2024 and presented at The New School for Social Research’s 2025 Anthropology Graduate Student Conference and Society for the Anthropology of Religion (SAR) Biennial Conference 2025. https://philosofree8.wordpress.com

about: Raised by a single mother who worked as a laborer in Vietnam and forging his learning path through the liberal arts, Ben (b. 2003) has been developing a photography-based practice that often reflects on the everyday and his evolving sense of self within it. His work explores the complexities of the human condition in relation to the authorship of representation and the social codes that often go unquestioned. Currently, he works as a creative freelancer, taking on various ad-hoc projects across filmmaking, photography, creative direction, curating, and producing and programming artistic initiatives and cultural programs. Full portfolio and resume available upon request. name: Uyen Thu Vu
about:
I’m Vu Thu Uyen, a Senior Communication Student at RMIT University Vietnam. In the journey of pursuing my Bachelor's Degree at RMIT, I have been trained in both Advertising and Public Relations streams. I spent most of the time practicing planning and innovating strategies to identify and solve problems for brands, companies, or organizations. Besides, I am also an active member of the Green Generation Club and other student communities at RMIT Vietnam.

In the very early stage of my professional journey, I had experience in content-centric jobs. In the communication field, I worked at Zing News VNG - one of the most visited news websites in Vietnam. Working as a part-time associate reporter and writer for the news agency, I’m the author of 10+ published lifestyle news articles in my 3-month internship.

As reviewed by my friends, my head is mostly on clouds but very serious when confronted with problems and creative solutions for business. I enjoy networking with stakeholders and work best to support the shared goals of my teams. My passion is to be a creative director in the future MarCom industry to help my client/company deliver appealing messages to the exact target audience.

Have a look at my projects and resumé,

Thanks a bunch,

Uyen.

about: Slow Monday blues, and hello to you, I'm Xiong Chang, perpetually sleepy but always ready for the next challenge. I'm the kind of person who finds enjoyment in deep dives—whether it's into textbooks, spreadsheets, or new experiences. A bit of a perfectionist at heart, I like to take my time, methodically dissecting problems and finding just the right solutions. Though I might seem laid-back (or maybe just a little drowsy 😴), I'm always quietly absorbing, analyzing, and striving for improvement. Although I enjoy the outcomes of learning, my relationship with school has been a bit abusive—late nights, lost sleep, and a growing caffeine addiction. Yet, every successful presentation, report, and competition result has made it all worth it. It’s this drive that led me to pursue my MBA right after my bachelor's, hungry for more knowledge and new challenges. Launching my career with SODA Hotel Management Platform as the Qualities and Innovations Coordinator, my journey towards hotel management has taken off—along with my growing appreciation for the Microsoft Suite! Working with a company that thrives on innovation, helmed by innovators like Alvaro and Jacobo, has reinforced my drive for continuous improvement. Their focus on perfection and staying ahead in this fast-changing industry constantly reminds me of the importance of research and adapting. I’m excited to embrace this mindset and evolve within the hospitality sector. If you're as curious as I am about exploring the ever-evolving landscape of hospitality and tourism, let’s connect—there’s always something new to learn, and I'd love to hear your take on it. Here’s to the slow but steady journey ahead!

about: I'm a dedicated engineer with a background in Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering, graduated from RMIT University. After that, I completed a 6-month internship as a Project Engineer, where I gained hands-on experience working with Building Management Systems (BMS) — including PLCs, chillers, HVAC, and system integration for smart building environments. Currently, I work as a SolidWorks Application Engineer at a company that is an official Dassault Systèmes reseller in Vietnam. In this role, I support clients in the design and manufacturing sectors by providing CAD/CAM/CAE solutions, offering technical consultation, training, and helping engineering teams optimize their product development process with SolidWorks and related tools. I’m passionate about connecting design with real-world application, and I enjoy working at the intersection of technology, engineering, and customer support. I’m continuously looking to grow and contribute to projects that bring innovation and efficiency to the industry.

projects: [{"description": "I conducted an in-depth study that confidently compares traditional defense approaches with emerging national security paradigms designed to tackle modern challenges like cyber threats, climate change, and hybrid warfare. By synthesizing best practices and pinpointing gaps, I developed actionable recommendations that will effectively foster adaptive and forward-thinking strategies for national security.", "end_date": "Jan 2025", "start_date": "Nov 2024", "title": "Comparative Analysis of National Security Strategies: Tradition Versus Modernity"}, {"description": "Our team of 3 (Brazilian, Taiwanese, and Vietnamese) conducted one of the first academic papers about the Doughnut Economic Framework in real-world applications, particularly in the apparel and/or fashion industry.The paper includes a sample size of about 8 companies, and the characteristics that we chose include large capital versus small size, international versus local brands, and companies with a good presence in sustainability marketing. We analysed using the content analysis method, which gathers official reports from companies and the industry. Meanwhile, for an objective assessment, we gathered critical analysis from experts within and outside the industry to provide a valuable and holistic understanding of what is happening from the outsiders' view.While fashion companies are adopting principles of Doughnut Economics through initiatives in circularity, resource management, and promoting sustainable consumer behaviors, significant critical gaps and challenges remain. Outsiders frequently perceive a lack of transparency and standardisation in sustainability efforts, leading to doubts that initiatives are genuine rather than mere marketing ploys, especially when specific data and scientific research are missing. Moreover, the industry struggles with consumer behaviour that often prioritises fast fashion trends and affordability over longevity and sustainability, while some performance-oriented products still necessitate materials that companies claim to avoid. This often translates into a perception that profit takes precedence over genuine ecological concerns, with sustainability measures potentially serving as marketing tools rather than core commitments, hindering systemic change and the full realisation of Doughnut Economics principles across the sector.", "end_date": "Jan 2025", "start_date": "Oct 2024", "title": "Analysis of Doughnut Economics Framework in the apparel industry (Expectations versus Reality)"}, {"description": "For my admission to the Aarhus Symposium 2024\u2019s Normal theme and Focus rounds, I crafted a paper that offers a unique approach to examining Denmark\u2019s national security strategy. Reflecting on the project, I take pride in how my significant contribution shaped our journey and led us to a more cohesive outcome and a High Distinction Grade for the Capstone Course.", "end_date": "May 2024", "start_date": "Apr 2024", "title": "Unlocking SME Potential: A Political Economy Perspective on Enhancing Added Value activities"}, {"description": "In my paper, I delved into Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI), a significant force in the Japanese economy and a leading solutions provider across energy, logistics, plants, and defence sectors. I used frameworks like Porter\u2019s Diamond, Five Forces, and Global Value Chain (GVC) models to analyse its international operations, including products, services, markets, and assets.I learned a lot, particularly about MHI's operational efficiency through its horizontal \"keiretsu\" model, fostering strong collaboration among Mitsubishi subsidiaries. I also discovered its global leadership in gas turbines with the highest market share and its strong supplier position with transformative technologies like the Carbon dioxide Capture, Utilisation, and Storage (CCUS) system. Analysing its GVC, I understood it as both relational and hierarchical, illustrating the Sniker value chain model prevalent in technology and capital-intensive industries.However, my paper also highlighted significant ongoing challenges. I explored the decarbonization feasibility of MHI\u2019s ambitious net-zero goal by 2040, noting that CCUS technology is still under development, the immense investment needed for heavy industry decarbonization (like steel), and the difficulty of integrating new tech with existing infrastructure, making short-term carbon neutrality impractical for many plants. Another key challenge is the volatile business environment, where geopolitical tensions lead to supply chain delays (currently 37% higher lead times than pre-pandemic) and decreased orders. A crucial takeaway was MHI\u2019s delicate task of balancing long-term growth, its net-zero mission, competitiveness, and financial performance.", "end_date": "Apr 2024", "start_date": "Feb 2024", "title": "Examining International Operations of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI): The Potential Challenges in International Markets"}, {"description": "In this report, I proposed a global mentoring program for the GM company for female expatriates and their host or home mentors, aiming to address pressing issues such as low satisfaction and high turnover rates among female expatriates and improve communication effectiveness between headquarters and subsidiaries. The program is structured around a four-component framework\u2014antecedents, inputs, outputs, and outcomes\u2014derived from the Logic model, Developmental Evaluation model, and the mentoring ecosystem. Key focus areas include providing psychological support, understanding external contexts, ensuring proper etiquette, and developing cultural competency. The program should support a mosaic mentoring approach, allowing a combination of mentoring types (e.g., co-mentoring, peer/group mentoring) to cater to diverse mentee needs and facilitate knowledge transfer. Crucially, matching mentors and mentees based on personality is emphasised to improve retention rates and psychological support that female expatriates particularly value. Furthermore, etiquette and cultural sensitivity training are essential for fostering effective intercultural mentoring relationships. For evaluation, I suggested using the Mentoring Competency Assessment (MCA) for outputs and the Developmental Evaluation model for outcomes, enabling effective communication of the program's impact and alignment with organisational goals, including SDG targets.During this process, I also identified a key weakness within my proposed program: the \"complicity of models\" used. This complexity could potentially \"confuse practitioners\" attempting to implement the program. Therefore, an area for improvement would be to provide \"more nuance in how and when each model/framework is applied in the dynamic employment-operations context\". This would help clarify the practical application of the integrated theoretical frameworks, making the program more accessible and actionable for those responsible for its execution.", "end_date": "Jan 2024", "start_date": "Dec 2023", "title": "A Comprehensive Global Mentoring Program: Enhancing Support and Retention for Female Expatriates"}, {"description": "The focal point of my team's report was an analysis of Singapore Port and Hai Phong Port, both essential trade hubs in ASEAN and globally, focusing on their operations, challenges, and recommendations for improvement. Singapore Port is known for its advanced operations, exceptional efficiency, and strategic location in the Strait of Malacca, a vital route for about 25% of global shipping. It continually invests in modern infrastructure like the Tuas Port, projected to be the world's largest fully automated port. In contrast, Hai Phong Port, the largest in Northern Vietnam, is crucial for accessing inland Vietnamese markets and benefits from its geographical location and increasing governmental investments.However, both ports face operational challenges. Hai Phong Port struggles with potential electricity outages, infrastructure effectiveness, and competition against foreign firms, particularly since 90% of its businesses are SMEs. While Singapore Port is advanced, it must adapt to changing environmental regulations, such as the sulphur quota, implement measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and invest in technologies like electric harbour boats. My team recommended that Hai Phong Port needs better coordination from authorities for power supply, enhancing multimodal capabilities in conjunction with dry ports, and managing intra-port competition. For Singapore Port, we suggested a comprehensive power management system to meet its net-zero targets and optimise operations.Reflecting on the paper's development, I believe it could have been improved with a more nuanced analysis of operational challenges and recommendations. Certain quantified statistics, though outside our research scope, would have better justified specific impediments. Lastly, a stronger correlation of the ports' advantages to broader macro factors would have enhanced understanding of their influences..", "end_date": "Jan 2024", "start_date": "Aug 2023", "title": "Singapore and Hai Phong Ports: Operations, Challenges, and Recommendations"}, {"description": "Our team\u2019s analysis of DatBike, a Vietnamese electric motorcycle manufacturer, reveals that Indonesia is a promising market for international expansion. With around USD 16.5 million in funding, DatBike can introduce a universal scooter model in Indonesia, known for its battery production, abundant nickel resources, and government support for the electric vehicle (EV) sector. The two-wheeled electric vehicle market is still developing, with a target of 13 million electric motorbikes on the road, especially needed given the severe air pollution in Jakarta.To enter this market, we recommend a Joint Venture (JV), starting with a Contractual JV in 2025 and evolving into a Vertical JV by 2030, perhaps partnering with Maka Motors. A Polycentric Approach for Human Resource Management would leverage local expertise. Emphasizing ESG principles is essential for making a positive impact and differentiating DatBike. Notably, design plays a key role for Indonesian consumers, suggesting that DatBike's retro style could resonate well.Despite some challenges during the project, we stayed committed. One issue was the lack of detailed information about the Indonesian EV bike market, leading us to make some assumptions. We also found limited insights on consumer design preferences. Additionally, we faced some teamwork hurdles that affected our workflow, and our presentation slides could have benefited from more professional design elements for better visual appeal..", "end_date": "Sep 2023", "start_date": "Aug 2023", "title": "DatBike Company Global Expansion Proposal"}, {"description": "As part of our group report for OMGT2085: Introduction to Logistics and Supply Chain Management, I conducted an in-depth analysis of Bao Bi Anh Sang Joint Stock Company (BBAS), a prominent packaging manufacturer in Ho Chi Minh City, specifically examining their rice packaging supply chain. My team and I meticulously explored BBAS's four primary operations: demand planning, procurement, production, and warehousing, and identified that the company primarily utilises a pull system, which supports customised packaging but can lead to production bottlenecks and delays when demand is uncertain. A significant challenge we uncovered was the \"significantly questioned information flow\" within their supply chain, which leads to uncertain demand planning, particularly exacerbated by the volatility of Vietnamese agriculture due to climate change. To address these issues and enhance resilience, I recommended adopting a hybrid (push-pull) supply chain model to proactively meet market demand and implementing a Collaborative Planning, Forecasting, and Replenishment (CPFR) system to boost information transparency, shorten lead times, and mitigate inventory expenses and the bullwhip effect. Additionally, we highlighted the importance of leveraging Industry 4.0 technologies, such as Internet of Things (IoT) for real-time tracking and Big Data analytics for informed decision-making, along with Climate-smart Agriculture (CSA) for their rice sector partners, to optimise operations and build resilience. This project was instrumental in solidifying my understanding of complex supply chain dynamics and practical problem-solving in logistics.", "end_date": "May 2023", "start_date": "Apr 2023", "title": "Optimising supply chain operations of Bao Bi Anh Sang JSC packaging product line"}, {"description": "The exercise I performed in this document involved researching and differentiating Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Corporate Sustainability. about: The complexities of the supply chain often go unnoticed, yet its impact on everyday life is profound. Most don’t realize the intricacies required to ensure that products reach the shelves—from raw materials to final delivery, each step plays a critical role. As a former Procurement Capacity Management Specialist at DHL Global Forwarding, I gained first-hand experience in the intricate logistics behind transporting high-stakes cargo. Working with industry giants like Apple and Dell, I managed shipments from Hanoi to destinations across the US and Asia, collaborating closely with airlines and teams to ensure precision in every movement. My passion lies in continuous learning and innovation within the logistics and supply chain field. With strong leadership and organizational skills, I strive to create value by opening new opportunities, enhancing team capabilities, and aligning efforts with organizational goals. I am excited to further my career in Logistics and Supply Chain Management and welcome connections from those who are in the field. Feel free to reach out at dnghalinh@gmail.com.

publications: [{"date":"September 22, 2023","description":"Objectives: To describe the current state and determine the requirements for continuing education (CE) of clinical nurses in Vinh Phuc province from 2019 to 2022. Subjects and method: A cross-sectional descriptive study, combining quantitative and qualitative, was conducted on 677 clinical nurses working in Vinh Phuc province from February 2022 to October 2022.Results: Although 100% of nurses participated in clinical training from 2019 to 2022 (n=677), only 39.6% attended the requisite number of sessions. The majority of training programs are short-term (52.3%); the training content is mostly technical skills and communication; training in scientific research accounts for just 30.7%. Most of the research subjects have training needs in Advanced Qualification (79.5%) and Nursing Technical Skills (69%). In which, the need for training in performing first aid techniques accounts for the highest rate (90.7%), followed by Ambu ball squeeze and extra-thoracic compression (73.1%). The Intubation Intubation Technique (87.9%) and the Intubation Assistance Technique (74.6%) have the greatest proportion of training demands among difficult nursing methods.Conclusion: Although 100% of nurses participated in the CME program, only 39.6% attended the requisite number of classes. The nursing program focuses on nursing technical skills, scientific research training, and a variety of complicated nursing procedures that have not before been focused on. Most nurses need training to advance their professional credentials, communication skills, and scientific research.Keywords: Continuing education, nurse, CE.","subtitle":"Vietnam Medical Journal","title":"Current Situation and Demand for Continuing Medical Education (CME) of Clinical Nurses in Vinh Phuc Province"},{"date":"July 19, 2023","description":"Art has long been an important subject of the education system. In Vietnam, teaching arts is taken a solid position as a subject of the education system from primary to tertiary education level. However, little is known about the situation and the need for transformation in the way students are trained to become art teachers. To clarify the view and attitudes of the to-be-an-art-teacher students, we conducted an online survey to collect data from students who enrolled in the bachelor course, majoring in art teaching at a university in Vietnam. A total of 57 students participated in the survey, most of them are females in the second year of the on-the-job B.A. course. The results showed that the respondents reported needing more diversified learning content such as applied arts, installation, and multimedia. They showed a need to have more practice sessions and fieldwork such as visiting museums and exhibitions. The respondents specified that they chose this major because they love the subject and love teaching, as well as to address the social need of learning arts, as arts seem to be a more important subject for elementary education. They shared a positive attitude toward the internationalization of local art education, however, none of them plan to study abroad. These findings imply the need for improving the quality of teaching and internationalization of art teacher education to meet international standards in the context of a developing country.","subtitle":"The International Academic Forum (IAFOR)","title":"Students’ Views of Art Education as Their Future Career"}]

name: Tiếu Dung (Jojo)
about: Tiếu Dung, or Jojo, often recalls a line from Winnie-the-Pooh: “𝘏𝘰𝘸 𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘦𝘵 𝘵𝘰 𝘣𝘦 𝘢 𝘤𝘭𝘰𝘶𝘥, 𝘧𝘭𝘰𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘯 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘣𝘭𝘶𝘦.” Jojo carries it as a quiet guide, a reminder to embrace change, seek perspective, and keep finding new ways to grow alongside the people she works with. Her career path hasn’t followed a fixed blueprint. Every step has been guided by a genuine commitment to people, learning from them, growing with them, and bringing out the best in teams. Jojo believes that when people thrive, the business thrives. Discovering her place in hospitality in 2021 marked the start of a journey where she has been able to channel that mindset into both client relationships and internal team development. With that foundation built, Jojo now works with clients across industries and markets worldwide at The Brand Promise, a Saigon-based boutique branding firm with a global reach 🌏. 𝘈𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘪𝘳𝘮 𝘨𝘳𝘰𝘸𝘴, 𝘪𝘵 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘷𝘦𝘴 𝘵𝘰 𝘶𝘱𝘩𝘰𝘭𝘥 𝘪𝘵𝘴 𝘷𝘪𝘴𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘧𝘶𝘵𝘶𝘳𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘬 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘷𝘢𝘭𝘶𝘦𝘴 𝘪𝘵 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘴𝘦𝘵 𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘵𝘰 𝘦𝘮𝘣𝘰𝘥𝘺. In the company’s first two years of operations, her role as Executive Assistant to the CEO gave her a front-row seat to strategic decision-making, cross-functional collaboration, and the daily balancing act between vision and execution. Now, as a Global Account Manager, Jojo carries forward those lessons with a sharper focus on building sustainable growth through meaningful partnerships and empowered teams. She remains in “treasure hunt” mode, always curious and always learning, knowing that the best results come from shared purpose, trust, and the journey taken to get there.

about: From the bustling halls of a normal student, with no special talents, academic awards, or activities prizes, I embarked on a journey that would test my resilience and determination. When I entered university, it felt like stepping into a different world. Around me were peers with significant awards and outstanding extracurricular achievements. The pressure was immense, and I found myself questioning: Could I really do it? Who am I in this vast world? What will I achieve? Despite the doubts and the overwhelming peer pressure, I chose to believe in myself. With unwavering perseverance and a steadfast belief in my abilities, I pushed forward. My efforts paid off when I joined Fulbright University Vietnam, a place that became the canvas for my ambitions. Here, I didn't just participate; I led. From participating in small activities of the Admissions Office, becoming a member, gradually being entrusted to lead a small team of 3-4 people, and now, I have officially been nominated as the Senior Admissions Student Assistant after just ONE YEAR of working, and now I am leading about more than 30 people. But my journey didn't stop there. With a spirit of wanting to contribute to the community I am studying in, I took on the role of President of the Fulbright Student Council for the academic year 2024-2025, where I spearhead initiatives to foster inclusivity and engagement within our student body. My experience extends to various projects, including the Humans of Fulbright Project and representing students as a Presidential Student Ambassador. Looking back over the years, from a student who knew almost nothing about extracurricular activities and had a CV far behind my peers, with perseverance and hard work, I have gained valuable lessons and made significant contributions. Through these experiences, I have honed my skills in management, strategic planning, and communication. I have learned that with determination and hard work, I can overcome any doubt and achieve great things. My story is a testament to the power of believing in oneself and the incredible journey that belief can take you on.

name: Lam Ha
about: I’m a driven university student at RMIT with a passion for student development, marketing, and educational support. My journey has led me through diverse roles—starting as a Teaching Assistant supporting students their English studies, then diving into marketing during my internship at The Bear Connection. There, I worked on SEO blog content, managed social media, built university partnerships for career workshops and events, and supported recruitment and translation tasks. Later, as a Peer Advisor at RMIT Global Experience, I had the privilege of consulting with over 400 students and their families on exchange opportunities, managing social media promotions, and supporting events that enriched student experiences. I also contributed to boosting participation in the RMIT Career Fair, helping to increase student engagement year over year. My passion lies in supporting students through their career development journeys. There’s no better reward than seeing someone succeed with a little guidance. I’m excited about future opportunities where I can continue to make a difference, whether through marketing, student support, or educational initiatives. Feel free to connect—I’m always open to sharing ideas and collaborating on new projects.

But the bigger picture – how systems are connected, how decisions ripple through and how innovation takes shape. My journey has taken me through lecture halls, into foreign countries, into hands-on practice, into chaos, into structure – and even led me to leave my home country to see the world through my own lens. publications: [{"description":"Service robots that work alongside humans in a shared environment need a navigation system that takes into account not only physical safety but also social norms for mutual cooperation. In this paper, we introduce a motion planning system that includes human states such as positions and velocities and their personal space for social-aware navigation. The system first extracts human positions from the LiDAR and the RGB-D camera. It then uses the Kalman filter to fuse that information for human state estimation. An asymmetric Gaussian function is then employed to model human personal space based on their states. This model is used as the input to the dynamic window approach algorithm to generate trajectories for the robot. Experiments show that the robot is able to navigate alongside humans in a dynamic environment while respecting their physical and psychological comfort.","subtitle":"Published in Proceedings 2024 International Conference on Control, Robotics and Informatics (ICCRI)","title":"Socially Aware Motion Planning for Service Robots Using LiDAR and RGB-D Camera"}]

Through business case competitions, marketing projects, and product management roles, I’ve honed the ability to connect data with commercial value, delivering recommendations that balance creativity and logic. As businesses increasingly rely on data as a core asset, I aspire to work at the forefront of strategy and analytics—helping organizations uncover growth opportunities and make smarter decisions through the power of data.

name: Cuong Nguyen
about: I am a final-year student pursuing a double major in Integrated Sciences (concentration: Health Science) and Psychology at Fulbright University Vietnam—the first and only liberal arts university in Vietnam. With a deep interest in both physical and mental health, I am particularly drawn to the Microbiome–Gut–Brain Axis (MGBA), which I intend to pursue further through graduate studies and academic research. Currently, I am interning at the Clinical Microbiology Lab of the Hospital for Tropical Diseases (Ho Chi Minh City), where I have gained valuable hands-on experience and inspiration for my undergraduate capstone project. This experience has solidified my passion for interdisciplinary health sciences and translational research. I aspire to contribute to science that bridges laboratory findings and human well-being — especially in understanding how gut health impacts the brain and behavior.

name: Chinenye Ekwebelem
about: Hi! Chinenye Susan Ekwebelem originally from Nigeria, is a dedicated individual with an ardent passion for healthcare which led her to pursue a nursing career in Vietnam. She is driven by a deep interest in public health and diseases of global significance. She has been actively involved in research, starting as an intern at NIMR (Nigerian Institute of Medical Research) and now as a Research Assistant at VinUniversity. Her work focuses on bridging healthcare and sustainability to create holistic, long-lasting solutions. Beyond research, she is fully committed to making a social impact through education, community-building, and sustainability efforts. As a volunteer with Keep Vietnam Clean, she is actively working to address pollution and raise awareness about environmental challenges in Vietnam. She strongly believes that environmental health is inseparable from healthcare, and tackling both issues is crucial to improving overall health outcomes. In the future, she aspires to lead a team of healthcare professionals to underserved regions in Nigeria, providing free medical care while integrating sustainability into healthcare delivery. She aims to create lasting change and uplift impoverished communities by addressing both medical and environmental needs.

name: Trang (Camellia) Đỗ
about: Never stop growing, never stop giving. Growing up under the protective care of my parents, I always felt safe and nurtured. This sense of security shaped my personality and character. However, deep within me was a strong desire to break free, to spread my wings, and live a life that was truly my own. I wanted to step out of my comfort zone and discover my authentic self. My growth journey has always been deeply intertwined with community and service. From a young age, I joined my parents in volunteer activities, helping those in need. As I grew older, my passion for supporting communities only intensified. However, I soon realized that my resources and finances alone were not enough to make a meaningful impact. Acknowledging this, I focused on learning, seizing every opportunity to develop my skills and knowledge. At Fulbright University, I connected with like-minded individuals who shared my vision of personal growth combined with community service. Together, we founded a project close to my heart: Braille Music Access—a project dedicated to supporting the visually impaired community. In every organization I’ve been a part of, I have prioritized initiatives centered on community service and the spirit of paying it forward. I firmly believe in returning the benefits I’ve received from society back to the community. This passion for making an impact extends to my professional aspirations. Whether through a community project or a workplace initiative, I am motivated by the belief that meaningful work is rooted in both positive customer experiences and a lasting influence on the community. For me, creating value isn’t just about individual success—it’s about how we collectively grow and uplift those around us. As I step forward in my journey, I’m excited to explore opportunities in Business, Marketing, and Hospitality. With a passion for innovation and service, I aim to continue growing while contributing to the communities I care about.

about: I am fond of writing fascinating stories, but I am disgusted writing stories following others' ideas. I live with my belief: "I am the writer, I write for myself, and I decide what to write". My very first passion, since I was a child, is writing and telling intriguing plots for my audience. Before I realised my enthusiasm, I thought I loved reading others' books as I found it wonderful to spend all day reading books. But I soonly lost all my interest when the contents did not surprise and excite me anymore due to their predictability. Hence, that was the time when I started composing fanfiction on Wattpad to satisfy my imagination. And surprisingly, my talent was exposed and obtained plenty of compliments. And that's when it happened. After my ability was recognised, I planned for my career path. I decided to pursue Communication where I can keep on my passion in my future job, as a Copywriting and Content Writer. At the beginning of my university life, I was working as a Content Writer in a club named Current Media to write social media posts and stories for a printed magazine. Besides, I have experienced writing scripts for postcards and articles for magazines in a couple of my courses. This reminds me of my passion and gift for creative writing. My specialities include teamworking, verbal and written communication, working under pressure and problem-solving. Besides, I have learned social listening and research from the university. So far I am able to utilise Microsoft Word, Excel and Powerpoints, while Adobe tools like Illustrator, Photoshop and Pro Premiere are in the learning process.

projects: [{"description": "This was a tough yet very meaningful research that we carried out for a year, with a hope to contribute to the reconciliation process after the Vietnam/American war.I and my friends studied the mental care systems for different groups of veterans from the Vietnam/American war. There were four groups included: Democratic Republic of Vietnam (DRVN) veterans, Republic of Vietnam (RVN) veterans currently living in Vietnam, RVN veterans living in the U.S, and American Vietnam veterans. The research was done with archival research and interviews with veterans, community leaders, and mental health professionals in Vietnam and the U.S.We discovered several systematic and cultural barriers keeping each group from reaching out to official mental care services. name: Trang Nguyen
about: Nice to meet you, My name is Trang Nguyen, a 2001-born author and creative based in Hanoi, Vietnam. As an undergraduate of Professional Communication at RMIT University, I spent some time exploring the marketing industry to enhance work-related skills, gain practical experiences and figure out the career path that fulfills my personal and professional goals. Since April 2023, I've been working as a copywriter and editor for Edmicro, an award-winning company specializing in AI-powered learning experiences and education. Currently, I taught myself 2D graphic designs and produced some visuals for Edmicro and other small-scale local businesses. Apart from that, I take pride in being a fiction author and poet with a newly published short stories collection. I'm the co-founder of Dòng-chữ (Lines or Flow of words), a literature-focused project for Vietnamese Gen Z who loves to read, write, connect and experiment on the beauty of language and the touch points of various art forms. In addition to that, I'm also a frequent contributor for e-magazines and newspapers, including credible names like Văn nghệ Quân đội, Phụ nữ TP.HCM, Elle Vietnam and Ngoisao. With an enthusiasm for creativity and arts, I'm learning everyday to incorporate fresh and original ideas/perspectives into both my writings and marketing contents. Thank you for reading! If you're interested, please feel free to reach me with contact information provided in this LinkedIN profile.

about: Thank you for stopping by my profile! This curiosity has shaped me into a generalist, someone who is comfortable working across different areas such as school services, weddings-events, and now FMCG. My passion lies in visual communication and community connection. I believe in the power of words and visuals working together, especially in events, to create meaningful engagement. Through content creation, activity planning, and shared experiences, I aim to spark interaction and leave a positive impact. The values that guide me are captured in three simple words: Connect. Create. Interact. As I step into my professional journey, I am looking forward to opportunities as a fresher or junior where I can find the right value match. If you share the same interests or values, I’d love to connect and have a chat!

name: Ngoc Doan Hong
about: My parents had doubts about creative careers — but they love and trust me. I still remember winning third prize in a district-level drawing contest back in third grade. It was a clumsy little drawing about family, but it planted the first seed of art in me. Still, for my parents, art never felt like a “safe” choice. They weren’t harsh, but they hoped I’d choose something more stable — like being a doctor, engineer, or accountant. I tried to meet that expectation, and so I chose Economics when I entered university. But I never felt at home among spreadsheets and office routines. I couldn’t imagine living a life that felt dull and draining. It took courage, but eventually I told my parents how I truly felt. Though worried, they chose to support me. And that’s how I found my way into design. I’m not someone who enjoys working alone. I love connecting with others. That’s why I joined clubs, volunteered, and even served as the president of a small student club. Through those experiences, I learned how to organize, collaborate, lead, and listen. I started gaining real-world design experience through internships at small design studios. There, I strengthened my skills in Illustrator and Photoshop, explored new tools like After Effects and Blender, and learned how to work with both clients and teammates. I’m currently seeking a full-time opportunity in the field of graphic design — a place where I can continue learning, contribute meaningfully, and grow with intention. I’m especially passionate about branding and social media design — where visuals don’t just communicate, but create emotion and build identity. My design style is adaptable, but often leans toward minimalism, brightness, and a youthful tone. One quote from The Pursuit of Happyness has always stayed with me: “If you ask me a question and I don't know the answer, I’ll tell you I don’t. But I bet you what — I know how to find the answer, and I will.” I’m far from perfect. There’s still so much I don’t know. But I believe that, day by day, I’m becoming better.
